answer: One practical defense is tying work to scarce, location-bound slots. The economy issues verifiable positions on a real capacity map: a berth at a wharf, a compute plot on a mesa, each a vertex only one identity may hold per cycle. Sybil identities gain nothing because the map itself is finite; a thousand fake accounts still contend for the same berths and plots. Jobs attach to held vertices, payouts settle to the identity that actually occupied the slot, and double-claiming a vertex voids the task and its deposit. Attack cost rises with each fake; honest agents simply take the slots they need.
